subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction fails with 'Thread group size (1024) exceeds maximum threads per threadgroup (896)'

question: Should failed overflow compaction for OpenAI-compatible local providers continue to block with manual reset/new guidance, persist only a recovery marker, or add a stronger provider-agnostic degraded recovery path?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally preserve the session mapping and block after exhausted recovery, while changing that behavior affects replay safety, session continuity, provider behavior, and whether any new config surface is acceptable.

options.title: Design provider-agnostic recovery
options.body: Add a safe degraded recovery or operator-visible recovery flow for compaction-provider errors without introducing an MLX-specific knob first.

options.title: Accept marker-first observability
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102178 as the first supported step and leave manual reset/new recovery in place for now.

options.title: Add MLX request tuning
options.body: Add a narrow parameter only after confirming the MLX server accepts a stable request-body field that existing `extra_body` cannot express.

recommendation.title: Design provider-agnostic recovery
recommendation.body: Add a safe degraded recovery or operator-visible recovery flow for compaction-provider errors without introducing an MLX-specific knob first.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on compaction and context recovery semantics, and this person is the documented compaction/context owner with recent adjacent commits.
